stem: Build a right-angled triangle in which $\cos\theta = {=t}$, where $\theta$ is the marked angle. Drag the two legs; a triangle of any size with this cosine is correct.
solution: Cosine compares the side adjacent to $\theta$ with the hypotenuse: $\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$.
Write the target ${=t}$ as a fraction of whole numbers, adjacent over hypotenuse: for example $0.8 = \frac{4}{5}$ and $0.6 = \frac{3}{5}$.
You drag the legs, not the hypotenuse. A hypotenuse of 5 with an adjacent leg of 4 leaves an opposite leg of 3 ($4^2 + 3^2 = 5^2$); with an adjacent leg of 3 the opposite leg is 4.
Check the live readout: $\cos\theta = {=t}$. Any enlargement of the triangle gives the same cosine, because only the ratio of the sides matters.
notes: Mirrors book Ex 5.1 Q1(b). used-sine is mapped to reads-sides-from-other-angle (opposite and adjacent swapped, so cos theta comes out as opposite over hypotenuse); it also fires on a plain SOH-CAH-TOA slip, which has no misconception of its own here. used-tangent can fire (cosine built as opposite over adjacent) but none of this objective's misconceptions names a cosine/tangent confusion (sine-as-opposite-over-adjacent is about sine), so it is left unmapped rather than forced; off-target likewise. Shares the 3-4-5 triangle with the sin template on purpose: cos 0.8 and sin 0.6 are the same triangle.
